record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: In fully decentralized federated learning without a central coordinator, how can stochastic-gradient-based training for deep models be made robust to temporary client unavailability, client dropout and joining, message loss, non-IID client data, heterogeneous update frequencies, and communication-topology choices, while still achieving good practical convergence time?

evidence.quote: Fully decentralized algorithms for learning should be robust to the limited availability of the clients (with clients temporarily unavailable, dropping out or joining during the execution) and limited reliability of the network (with possible message drops). While for the special case of generalized linear models, schemes using the duality structure could enable some of these desired robustness properties [231], for the case of deep learning and SGD this remains an open question. ... Additional open research questions concern non-IID data distributions, update frequencies, efﬁcient communication patterns and practical convergence time [443].

artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (e.g., DeceFL 2023, asynchronous decentralized FL with persistent dropout 2025) provide partial progress: convergence guarantees for convex/strongly-convex objectives or empirical mitigation strategies for specific subsets of the listed challenges. However, no algorithm is known that simultaneously handles all of (temporary unavailability, dropout/joining, message loss, non-IID data, heterogeneous update frequencies, topology effects) for deep non-convex SGD with provable robustness and good practical convergence time. The problem is broadly regarded as still open.

status_evidence.title: DeceFL: a principled fully decentralized federated learning framework
status_evidence.snippet: DeceFL relies only on local information transmission between clients and their neighbors; convergence rate O(1/T) for smooth strongly convex losses, with experiments on non-IID data.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial progress in fully decentralized FL but does not address the full set of robustness challenges for deep non-convex SGD.

status_evidence.title: Mitigating Persistent Client Dropout in Asynchronous Decentralized Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Persistent client dropout in asynchronous decentralized FL is difficult because asynchronicity and decentralization obfuscate information about model updates; proposes adaptive reconstruction strategies.
status_evidence.claim: Recent 2025 work confirms client dropout in fully decentralized FL is still an active, unresolved research problem.

status_evidence.title: Stabilizing and Improving Federated Learning with Non-IID Data and Client Dropout
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses instability of FedAvg-style training under highly non-IID data combined with client dropout.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the combination of non-IID data and dropout remains an open empirical/theoretical challenge.
